item.text: {"searches":[{"reason":"Develop paired sequence interventions that test whether recommendations depend on recent behavior and repeated narrow preferences. Compare recent-item masking, old-item masking, and order shuffling against matched random perturbations; measure ranking changes and validate their relationship to per-category validation HR@10. This would reveal when the sequence encoder ignores current intent without treating sensitivity alone as evidence of quality.","query":"sequential recommendation temporal shortcut learning diagnostic probes recent history masking order permutation matched controls ranking sensitivity 2024 2025 2026"},{"reason":"Build a practical failure taxonomy from available titles, descriptions, and histories: broad semantic association, supported complementarity, explicit compatibility conflict, and possible redundant purchase. Investigate evidence-backed hard-negative comparisons and an unknown state when prerequisites or purchase needs cannot be established. These probes could connect user feedback to score errors and targeted sampling or loss changes without inventing ownership, ratings, or preferences.","query":"recommendation diagnostic benchmark semantic hard negatives accessory compatibility prerequisites redundant purchases evidence grounded uncertainty abstention product titles descriptions 2024 2025 2026"},{"reason":"Establish whether diagnostic signals predict useful model changes rather than merely describe training fit. Research popularity- and history-length-controlled probes, exposure-normalized failure rates, paired bootstrap uncertainty, and agreement between sampled-candidate and full-catalog rankings. Use fixed training-history audits and validation-only comparisons across all four datasets, accounting for the small qualitative user sample and shared compute budget.","query":"recommender diagnostic metric validation sampled evaluation full catalog ranking disagreement popularity confounding paired bootstrap intervention model selection 2024 2025 2026"}]}
